summary_paraphrase: A meerkat who adores its yellow hat finds it gone and asks four animals in turn whether they ate it; each says no and names its own food, until the picture shows the zebra eating flowers off the very hat. The zebra apologises, the two make matching new hats, and every suspect ends up at one sunset picnic.

beats.function: same question, rising impatience in the picture
wordless picnic of the whole cast

characters.name: meerkat (unnamed)
characters.fear: that the hat is lost for good
characters.change: from accuser to friend sharing a matching hat
characters.tension_source: its rising anger, shown only in the pictures

characters.name: zebra (unnamed)
characters.change: from unknowing culprit to apologising friend
characters.humor_source: denies eating hats while eating one

humor_notes: Built on animal food habits and alliterative food lines, then on irony: the zebra denies eating hats while the picture shows it eating the hat under its flowers. Small visual jokes (a porcupine's wristwatch).

repetition.description: the same question and the same denial on four spreads, each ending with a new food line
repetition.why: the listener can join the question and denial after one round, and the fourth round breaks the pattern through the picture

repetition.description: the opening declaration of love for the hat returns at the end, now about the new hat and shared by two speakers
repetition.why: it closes a circle and turns a solo line into a shared one

notes: OBSERVED: the answer to the mystery is in the picture one spread before the text says it (the hat under the zebra's flowers).
OBSERVED: the protagonist's feelings (alarm, impatience, anger, shock) are carried only by the drawings; the text stays flat and repetitive.
OBSERVED: two wordless spreads, a face-to-face pause and the hat-making, carry the turn and the solution.
OBSERVED: the last story page is a wordless picnic of the whole cast at sunset.

strengths: a repeated question the listener can join after one round
the picture lets the reader solve the mystery before the hero
apology and making something together as the repair, not punishment
weaknesses: as text alone the reveal is lost: the zebra's line reads as another innocent denial
no animal is named, so a listener without pictures cannot tell the suspects apart
the zebra's innocence (not knowing it was a hat) is inferred from a face only

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: No peril or frightening imagery; the conflict is a lost possession and is repaired by apology and making a new hat together. Peak is research intensity 4 of 5 on one page, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale. The reveal depends on the picture (MagicPaper stories are text-only today).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
